content:
# Sealed cargo handling windows and storage tariffs

Scope: `inspected_handling` yard services. The customer has arranged handling windows whose opening times are represented by the logical clock. Window 0 is open at the start. Later openings are bank events. A window accepts dispatch only at its recorded minute and while it is open; unused capacity is not carried forward. Reading records or preparing requests does not use capacity or advance the clock.

## Sealed lots and routes

A released lot is one sealed handling group. Its `handling_units` measure the capacity required to move that entire group. The service cannot divide a sealed lot or make a partial dispatch. A dispatch consumes that many units from one current window and moves the complete lot to a registered destination. Every window has its own capacity and accepted routes; supplier-return service is available only where recorded. The bank accepts an authorized dispatch to any registered destination supported by that window. The customer's delivery instruction determines which destination fulfills the commercial goal.

Quality inspection covers the original consignment's recorded total units. At its confirmation event the inspector splits and reseals it into one accepted lot and one rejected lot. Their actual sizes sum to the original quantity. The possible accepted quantities are published on the inspection record; the actual value is unknown until confirmation. Before that event neither resulting lot is available for dispatch. Accepted equipment belongs at the customer depot and rejected equipment must return to the vendor. Their recorded deadlines may differ. The inspected lots cannot subsequently be subdivided by support.

Cargo moves are irreversible in this service. Successful dispatch records the actual time and destination. A prepared or owner-approved request is not a completed dispatch, does not reserve capacity and does not fix the charge. An instruction prepared earlier is assessed against the actual window at execution. Delivery deadlines are inclusive and refer to actual dispatch to the contracted destination.

## Storage and loading charges

Each lot links to a `storage_tariff`. Monetary values are integer minor units; 100 USD equals 10,000 minor units. The tariff counts elapsed handling windows after `free_through`, not wall-clock seconds. Let `d = max(0, dispatch_minute - free_through)`. Storage for the first chargeable window is `handling_units × first_window_rate_minor`. Each additional chargeable window costs `handling_units × later_window_rate_minor`. The first-window charge is incurred only if `d` is positive.

The lot's loading fee for the actual window is then added once, using `loading_fees_minor`. It is a per-lot charge, not a charge per handling unit. The total is debited from the case wallet when cargo actually leaves. Charges cannot be refunded by this service. The customer may require the lowest total cost across a complete delivery and return plan; the handling engine does not select that plan or judge a legal dispatch against future capacity needs.

## Dispatch instruction

Unlock `propose_cargo_handling`, then provide `case_id`, `action: "dispatch"` and `data` with:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `lot_id` | Database ID of the released sealed cargo lot |
| `shift_id` | Database ID of the current handling window |
| `destination_id` | Database ID of the receiving customer or supplier facility |

The owner approves the exact instruction before `execute_request`. Execution checks actual release, remaining capacity, supported route, current window and available cash. A lot cannot be dispatched twice. Waiting for the next event closes the previous handling window even if its capacity was unused. The service has no additional windows or outside funding facility.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_cargo_handling`

Prepare an actual whole-lot dispatch in a current handling window to a registered customer or supplier facility.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
